description:
Measured 2026-08-13 while doing op-uyi3, in tampines-steam-tables, release.

crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/math/minimise.rs argues in its module doc that switching from recompute-both to probe reuse perturbs results at the ~1e-16 relative level, and quantifies the effect only on the BRACKET WIDTH (2.334157e-6 relative at k=80, '4e-22 absolute'), concluding it 'has no effect on the accuracy of the answer'.

The conclusion is right. The magnitude is understated for the LOCATED ABSCISSA, which is what callers actually consume.

Measured in tampines-steam-tables by running both forms side by side over 158 real IAPWS-IF97 golden-section searches (tests/golden_section_shared_search.rs::probe_reuse_moves_the_choke_far_below_the_stopping_rule), all three bracket shapes, 1 Pa stopping rule, brackets of order 1e5-1e7 Pa:
  worst |dp*|      = 5.990479e-1 Pa
  worst |dp*|/p    = 4.604111e-8
  worst |dG*|/G    = 3.429708e-13
and across the crate's full Zaloudek suite the largest observed move was 3 Pa on a 10.356 MPa choke (2.9e-7 relative).

That is ~8 orders larger than the 1e-16 the module doc implies, and it is the expected behaviour rather than a bug in the algorithm: a last-bit difference in a probe position can flip the comparison on a near-flat objective, or change which iteration first trips the stopping test, and the returned midpoint then shifts by up to about the stopping-bracket width. The answer stays within the tolerance the caller asked for -- which is the honest claim -- but 'differs in the last bits' is not.

Suggested fix: in the module doc's probe-reuse section, separate the two claims. (1) bracket width deviates from W0*gr^k by up to 2.3e-6 relative at k=80 (already measured, keep). (2) the LOCATED ABSCISSA can differ between the two forms by up to ~the requested x-tolerance, not by ~eps; add a measurement on MinSettings-scale tolerances rather than inferring it.

This bead is a documentation-accuracy issue, not a request to change the algorithm: probe reuse is the correct form and should stay. Filed from tampines-steam-tables, which was not permitted to edit outram-foam-basic-lib in that session.
title: outram-foam-basic-lib minimise.rs understates probe-reuse deviation: measured up to the stopping-bracket width, not 1e-16

acceptance_criteria: expand_to() returns a physically valid HemSteamCv outlet plus shaft power for both superheated and wet inlet states; wetness correction applied and documented; no NotYetImplemented remains.
description:
crates/tampines/src/components/turbine.rs:38 — expand_to() returns NotYetImplemented. It needs: isentropic outlet enthalpy via a real (p,s) flash on HemSteamCv (= TampinesSteamTableCV), then the efficiency correction, giving outlet state and shaft work W = mdot * eta_ad * (h1 - h2s).

Constant adiabatic_efficiency is not adequate at the LP end, which runs wet: apply a Baumann wetness correction (roughly 1 percent efficiency lost per 1 percent mean wetness) rather than a fixed Ratio.

Note the workspace convention: arrays default to (p,h) flashing because it carries phase data; a (T,p) single-phase flash panics on two-phase. The isentropic leg here is (p,s), which must land back on a (p,h) state.

Underlying isentropic/Schultz algebra already exists in outram_park_fork_dwsim_libs::expander::isentropic.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md section 1 and 3.1.
title: tampines Turbine: implement expand_to() — IF97 (p,s) isentropic flash + Baumann wetness correction

description: multi_region::outer_iteration::RegionModel currently realises Neutronics(LumpedNeutronics/point-kinetics), ThermalHydraulics(LumpedThermal), and Prescribed. When the mesh-based genfoam::neutronics diffusion/SP3/SN and genfoam::thermal_hydraulics solvers land (op-p6p.6/.7), add them as RegionModel variants and wire their correct()/residual into the Picard loop (the enum is exhaustive so every match site flags). Also unblocked: TM meshDisp source region.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: Done. Added mesh-based RegionModel variants in multi_region/mesh_region.rs: MeshNeutronics wraps the real DiffusionNeutronics (op-p6p.6) with cross-section (Doppler) temperature feedback via XS re-materialization at the importance-weighted mean TFuel each Picard iterate; MeshThermalHydraulics is a per-cell backward-Euler fuel-energy balance (thermal time-constant tau formulation) that is the integration seam for the full thermal_hydraulics::solver (op-p6p.7). Both wired into MultiPhysicsSolver via enum dispatch (RegionModel::MeshNeutronics/MeshThermalHydraulics; exhaustive match arms in outer_iteration.rs). V&V: mesh Doppler lowers k_eff (3.000->2.700 at 900->1800K); power-density conserved across a 20-cell->8-cell CellVolumeWeight map (rel 2.3e-16); coupled steady state settles at 909.8K with feedback -9.8 pcm and k_eff 2.9953. Fixed a cold-start false-convergence in the Picard loop (coupled >1-region needs >=2 sweeps). 24 multi_region tests pass release; Android check clean.

title: genfoam multiRegion: dispatch mesh-based Neutronics/TH/TM RegionModel variants

description:
outram-park-digital-twin-engine/examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/primary_loop.rs line 229 has a bare local `let mu = 3.5e-5;` (Pa s) inside HeliumPrimaryLoop::update_hydraulics, used to form the Reynolds number for a Darcy-Weisbach/Haaland pressure drop.

This is a defect: the real Arp-McCarty-Friend (NIST TN-1334) helium viscosity correlation is available in outram-park-fork-coolprop and is now wrapped, uom-typed and tested, in tampines::gas_phase::properties::helium_viscosity(T, p) (landed 2026-08-11 under op-jyyp.12).

Measured 2026-08-11 with the new adapter, helium at 3.0 MPa:
  250 C: mu = 2.932973e-5 Pa s
  450 C: mu = 3.676616e-5 Pa s
  700 C: mu = 4.531067e-5 Pa s
The hardcoded 3.5e-5 is therefore ~19 % high at the core inlet and ~23 % low at the core outlet -- it is not a defensible constant across the HTR-10 core range. (Unlike c_p, which really does vary by only 0.0034 % over the same range.)

Fix: replace the constant with tampines::gas_phase::properties::helium_viscosity, or use gas_phase::pipe::GasDuct directly, which does the friction and heat transfer with real properties.

Scope note: this bead is about the digital-twin-engine crate only; the tampines-side replacement path already exists and is tested. Related to op-wqk.9.1, which covers the broader placeholder-correlation cleanup in that example.
title: htgr_sim_v1: hardcoded constant helium viscosity 3.5e-5 Pa s -- replace with tampines gas_phase::properties

description:
Observed 2026-08-11 ingesting EUR 28712 EN (JRC HTR safety book, 264 pages) with kovan lit import. Command run:

./target/release/kovan lit import ~/Downloads/kjna28712enn.pdf --json-out crates/kovan-literature/open/reports/vhtr-modul-safety-jrc.json --markdown-out crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/open/vhtr-modul-safety-jrc.md

The Markdown body extraction was GOOD — 264 pages, 5373 lines, 498k chars, content intact. The METADATA was wrong in five ways, all of which had to be hand-patched afterwards:

1. TITLE TRUNCATED AT A LINE BREAK. Got "The High Temperature"; the actual title is "The High Temperature Gas-cooled Reactor: Safety considerations of the (V)HTR-Modul". The cover sets the title across three lines and only the first was taken.
2. EDITOR MISTAKEN FOR AUTHOR. Got authors = [Scheuermann, Walter], who is the first EDITOR. The actual authors are Kugeler, K., Nabielek, H. and Buckthorpe, D., listed above the editors on the cover. There is no editor field in KovanDocument at all, which is part of the problem — consider adding one.
3. document_type = Other, though the document carries strong Report markers: an EUR number, a JRC catalogue number, an ISSN and a Publications Office imprint. A heuristic on "EUR NNNNN EN" or "JRC NNNNNN" would catch this class.
4. source_sha256 left null even though the tool has the file open. It should hash what it ingests — provenance under DATA_POLICY.md wants it, and it is free to compute.
5. slug derived from the wrong author, giving scheuermann2017the — which also shows the truncated-title bug feeding into slug generation.

Also note: doi, year, page_count and visibility were all extracted CORRECTLY, so the extractor is not broadly broken, just weak on multi-line cover layouts and author/editor blocks.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION: for the title, join consecutive large-font cover lines rather than taking the first. For authors, prefer the block above an "Editors:" label when one is present. For document_type, add report-identifier heuristics. Always populate source_sha256.

Not urgent — hand-patching the JSON is quick and lit bibtex round-trips correctly afterwards. But every ingested document currently needs a manual metadata pass, which will not scale.
title: kovan-literature: lit import metadata extraction is unreliable on EU/JRC report PDFs
